articles.title: What happens to your pets when you die?
articles.summary: Without a proper plan – whether in a trust or will – your beloved companion could face an animal shelter or worse. The idea of making a will may be uncomfortable, but routine. Ensuring that your family and estate is taken care of is a kindness.
body: Sometimes, “somebody wants to set up a trust with substantial money in it”, he said. But more typically, the client wants to ensure “the right person” gets the dog or cat – but has no idea how best to do it.
As the person in charge of your pet’s livelihood, you can (and should) try to get something on paper that makes sense.

“Pets rely entirely on human care. Without a plan, they face stress, shelter, surrender or unnecessary euthanasia during an already chaotic time,” said Peter Klein, the founder of the therapy referral website Seek a Psych and a London-based cognitive behavioral therapist in private practice.

According to a report from Best Friends Animal Society, a non-profit advocacy group working to achieve no-kill statuses for shelters around the United States, 12.4% of the 4.74 million cats and dogs that entered the shelter system in 2025 ended up there due to owner illness or death.
points: Without a proper plan – whether in a trust or will – your beloved companion could face an animal shelter or worse.

articles.title: Privileged and proud: how nepo babies took fashion month by storm
articles.summary: From commanding the catwalks to acting as plus-ones for their famous parents, celebrity kids are bang on trend. Knee-length skirts and bras worn as tops were two of the main takeaways from fashion month, which wrapped up this week. But the biggest trend had nothing to do with clothing.
body: John Travolta’s daughter, Ella Bleu, 26, made her Paris catwalk debut at Miu Miu. Apple Martin, 22, the daughter of Chris Martin and Gwyneth Paltrow, walked the Chloé show.

Meanwhile, the Vogue World event in Milan featured the Italian tenor Andrea Bocelli’s son Matteo, 29, Nick and Susie Cave’s son Earl, 26, Ava Phillippe, 27, the daughter of the actors Reese Witherspoon and Ryan Phillippe, and many more nepo babies in attendance.
Mark Borkowski, a PR consultant, described the nepo baby phenomenon as “a wonderful cocktail of youth, nostalgia and inherited glamour”.

Fran Hoepfner, the author of The Field Guide to Nepo Babies, said it was vital that a nepo had both a family connection and a direct or adjacent industry connection. “Simply having rich parents does not automatically make someone a nepo baby,” she said. “It just makes you lucky.”

articles.title: I hitchhiked from Sydney to Perth, and found comfort in the company of strangers
articles.summary: The lost practice of hitchhiking is a subculture, an art, and a way of travel that satisfies wanderlust like no other trip. Plus, it costs nothing. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email. I’m alone, hunched over by a dusty road junction, and feeling the bite of the morning sun.
body: Most drivers who pass wave or give me a thumbs up. One gives me the finger. There isn’t much traffic. Someone tosses a water bottle out their window at me.

Just as I start to catastrophise in the dust, a four-wheel-drive quietly pulls off the road and comes to a stop behind me. I hoist my backpack around my shoulder, run over and jump in the passenger seat, thanking the driver profusely.

One of my stranger interests is hitchhiking. I’m drawn to the idea of abandoning control and finding comfort in a stranger’s company. It’s a subculture, an art, and a way of travel that satisfies wanderlust like no other trip. Plus, it costs nothing.

Once a popular way to travel in the 70s and 80s, these days it’s pretty rare to see a hitchhiker on the side of Australian roads. For starters, its reputation was overwhelmingly tarnished by its association with serial killer Ivan Milat, who murdered several hitchhikers in the early 90s. Australia is also one of the few countries in the world that make it legally fraught to hitchhike, with laws explicitly naming hitchhiking as an offence, though legislation differs between state and territories.
points: The lost practice of hitchhiking is a subculture, an art, and a way of travel that satisfies wanderlust like no other trip.

Most drivers who pass wave or give me a thumbs up.

articles.title: Paul Barry: ‘People should not be off limits’
articles.summary: The investigative journalist and former Media Watch host on staring down Alan Bond, the ‘scandal’ of steel tycoon Sanjeev Gupta, and the benefits of having six children. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email. It’s a hot and hazy morning in Sydney’s La Perouse.
body: He has chosen the Henry Head walking track as our stomping ground. “It’s a very restful place,” he says. “You can often see whales breaching.”

Barry plays golf at the New South Wales Golf Club, found within the national park. He was once the captain of the golf team at Oxford University, but then he “didn’t play for about 30 years”. He says: “I’ve had too many kids. It’s a very unsociable thing to do.”

The former Media Watch host, now 74, has six children, aged 21 to 48. Barry moved to Australia from the UK 40 years ago as “a bit of an adventure”, but he says he was also frustrated by his lengthy commute from a village in the Cotswolds to London, where he worked at the BBC on Newsnight and Panorama.

“Then when I got here I thought: you can do both!” he says. “You can work and live near the beach, have a family – and see your family. The weather’s good, the people are nice and the place is gorgeous. So why go back?”

articles.title: Cheers to the Nominees! The CFDA Board of Directors Toasted to the 2026 Fashion Award Contenders
articles.summary: Michael Kors hosted the annual Board of Directors dinner on Thursday evening at Café Zaffri, joined by a whole host of industry figures and upcoming CFDA Fashion Award nominees.
body: Kors, who is once again up for the American womenswear designer of the year accolade, was joined by fellow category nominees Rachel Scott and Wes Gordon, as well as menswear designer of the year nominees Willy Chavarria, plus Dao-Yi Chow and Maxwell Osborne of Public School New York. The future of American fashion was also well represented: Colleen Allen donned one of her own designs, as did CFDA/ Vogue Fashion Fund finalists Zane Li, Julia Ferentinos, and Emily Dawn Long, who are all recognized in the Google emerging designer of the year category. Jewelry designer Ana Khouri was in attendance, too.

With a resounding cheer from the room, Kors passed the microphone off and dinner was served. Over a refreshing crudo and endive salad, Vera Wang laughed with Lance LePere. Linda Fargo, recipient of this year’s Founder’s Award, and Chavarria posed for a quick snap, while Joseph Altuzzara and former CFDA president Stan Herman struck up a conversation near the burl leather bar.
All things considered, it was a fitting, and fashionable, warm-up ahead of the industry’s big night out on November 2.

articles.title: 20 Beautiful Drinking Glasses to Upgrade Your Everyday Glassware
articles.summary: It's time to replace those chipped, cloudy tumblers you've had for far too long.
body: A few weeks ago, I found myself meandering through my local Target (as a gal in her thirties with time to kill will do). Since it was nearly fall, I headed straight to the seasonal section to browse the early drop of cozy candles, throw blankets, and other autumnal home essentials. As I made my way to the kitchen aisle to dig through the mugs and festive cups, I saw it: a pumpkin-printed Anthropologie Icon juice glass staring back at me across the shelf. Only we weren’t anywhere near an Anthropologie, and we were still weeks out from Halloween.

I was overcome with confusion (I was at Target, right?), disappointment, and, dare I say, a little bit of rage. I left that day still thinking about that damned juice glass. Why had this $8 dupe pushed me over the edge? What was it about this stupid thing, which I’d seen zillions of times in one pattern or another, that pissed me off so much??
Well, therein lies the answer. I believe we’ve gone too far with the Anthropologie Icon juice glass. As a society, we need to rein it in and buy, literally, ANYTHING else. I’m begging you.
points: It's time to replace those chipped, cloudy tumblers you've had for far too long.

articles.title: Even When Emma Grede Throws a Dinner Party at Her Home, She Means Business
articles.summary: If you know anything about entrepreneur Emma Grede, you know she is all business, all of the time. So what does it look like when she needs to switch gears to hostess mode and show her guests a good time?
body: “I always think that if I’m using my time and my energy to be somewhere, I either want to be learning, making a useful connection, or figuring out a problem. I’m always after something,” Grede told Vogue. That thought process forms the premise behind A Seat at the Table, her reoccurring dinner series, where the line between entertaining and doing deals is deliberately blurred.

On a balmy mid-week evening in Los Angeles, Grede welcomed a bevy of similarly time-strapped founders including Elsa Hosk, Ashley Tisdale, Rachel Zoe, Shay Mitchell, Aurora James, and Pia Mance to her Bel Air home, alongside founders and executives from brands like Fishwife, Arrae, and Cymbiotika.

The party followed earlier editions in Los Angeles, New York, and Atlanta, and most recently London, where Grede was on her home turf for the opening of the new Skims store on Regent Street. The concept has been the same each time: seat interesting women together and let the conversation do the rest.

articles.title: 15 Retinol-Rich Foods to Stimulate Collagen and Your Immune System
articles.summary: A doctor weighs in on everything you need to know about the trendy “retinol” diet.
body: Anybody who is serious about anti-aging is using retinol in their beauty routine. The ingredient, which is a derivative of vitamin A, is considered the gold-star anti-aging ingredient when it comes to skin health. Vitamin A—whether it’s in the form of retinol or one of the other retinoids, like retinoic acid or retinyl palmitate—has been clinically proven to smooth lines, clear acne, and reverse sun damage because it supports cellular turnover.

But vitamin A doesn’t just come in a tube. There are plenty of foods that are rich in vitamin A, which is almost totally bioavailable and benefits more than just your skin. Eating a diet rich in vitamin A helps to support healthy immune and reproductive systems; when you’re applying it topically, it’s solely focused on dermal cellular turnover.

“Diet plays a significant role in our skin’s health and appearance,” says Manhattan-based board-certified dermatologist Dendy Engelman, MD, FAAD. “There are studies to support that increased vitamin intake helps skin in both the aging space and acne.”
Here’s how you can take advantage of vitamin A in your diet to improve your skin, immune system, and more.

body: Where the Pro Series OLED makes a stronger case for itself is gaming —its 120Hz refresh rate, VRR support, and AMD FreeSync Premium help keep fast-moving games looking smooth, with this PCMag review measuring an input lag of just 4.8 milliseconds at 1080p/120Hz and 8.8 milliseconds at 4K/60Hz, earning it the publication’s Lab Award for lowest input lag. That translates to very little delay between pressing a button and seeing the action onscreen, which is especially useful in racing games and competitive shooters. You also get four HDMI ports and support for Dolby Vision, HDR10, HDR10+, and HLG, although Nvidia G-Sync support is absent.

Outside gaming, the TV runs Roku’s own OS, whose straightforward interface puts your streaming apps front and center without burying them beneath endless recommendations—and it supports nearly every major streaming service except Twitch, along with AirPlay for casting from an iPhone, iPad, or Mac. Beyond streaming, you get Wi-Fi 5 for wireless connectivity and an ATSC 1.0 tuner for watching over-the-air broadcasts, although one convenience that's missing is hands-free voice control, so you'll need to use the remote for voice commands.
